title: Cas9-targeted long-read sequencing in Globodera pallida and Globodera rostochiensis
author: Sonawala, Derevnina, et al.
materials: Qubit dsDNA high sensitivity quantitation kit

This step describes the protocol for extracting HMW DNA from potato cyst nematode J2s. It has been adapted from the following protocol: https://www.pacb.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/SharedProtocol-Extracting-DNA-usinig-Phenol-Chloroform.pdf.7.Homogenize and digest J2s for DNA extraction.a.Add 20 μL of lysis buffer to the frozen J2 pellet and grind with a micro-pestle for ∼30 s until the pellet has thawed.b.Add 140 μL of lysis buffer and 40 μL of proteinase K. Mix by inversion.c.Incubate at 55°C for 18 h, mixing gently but often.8.Eliminate RNA.a.Add 10 μL of RNase A (10 mg/ml, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.b.Label this as tube 1.9.First extraction.a.Add an equal volume of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol solution to the lysed J2s (usually 200 μL).b.Either vortex tube for 1 min or rotate on a HulaMixer sample mixer for 15 min. The latter is preferred to retain the integrity of HMW DNA.c.Spin the tube at >10,000 × g for 5 min.d.Remove ∼180 μL of the top aqueous solution and place it into a new tube (tube 2).CRITICAL: Avoid touching or disturbing any of the phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol phase.Note: To retain the integrity of HMW DNA as much as possible, it is important to pipette the aqueous phase gently. It is also preferable to cut the ends of a P1000 pipette tip before using it to pipette the aqueous phase.10.Second Extraction:a.Add 200 μL of the elution buffer to the original tube 1 containing phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol phase.b.Either vortex tube for 1 min or rotate on a HulaMixer sample mixer for 15 min.c.Spin the tube at >10,000 × g for 5 min.d.Remove ∼180 μL of the top aqueous solution from tube 1 while avoiding any of the phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol phase. Add it to the previously collected aqueous solution in tube 2.11.Third extraction/ back extraction:a.Add equal volumes of the chloroform/isoamyl alcohol solution (usually ∼360 μL) to tube 2.b.Either vortex tube 2 for 1 min or rotate on a HulaMixer sample mixer for 15 min.c.Spin tube 2 at high speed for 5 min.d.Remove as much of the top aqueous solution as possible while avoiding the chloroform/isoamyl alcohol solution and place it into a new tube, tube 3.12.Genomic DNA precipitation:a.Add NH4OAc to tube 3 to a final concentration of 0.75 M. Add 1 μL of glycogen (Thermo Fisher Scientific, 20 mg/ml). Mix the solution well. Add 2.5X volume of 100% ethanol and mix well.b.Spin for 20 min in a 4°C centrifuge at top speed. Decant the supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.c.Wash the pellet by adding 300 μL of 80% ethanol (prepared fresh) and flicking the tube.d.Spin for 15 min in a 4°C centrifuge at top speed.e.Decant the supernatant and repeat step 12.c-12.d to wash the pellet a second time.f.Decant the supernatant and use a P20 pipette to carefully remove excess 80% ethanol. Allow the pellet to air dry for ∼30 min.g.Resuspend the pellet in 25–30 μL of elution buffer. Allow the pellet to resuspend overnight at 4°C.13.Quality and quantity assessment:a.Test the purity of the genomic DNA by measuring the ratio of absorbances at 260/280 nm and 260/230 nm using Nanodrop (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The ratios for genomic DNA with high purity should be between 1.8-2.0 and 2.0–2.2, respectively (see troubleshooting problem 2).b.Measure the amount using a fluorometric quantification method such as Qubit by following the manufacturer’s protocol (Thermo Fisher Scientific).

steps.title: Collect and wash J2s
steps.instruction: Collect second‑stage juvenile (J2) nematodes, wash them in 0.01 % Tween 20, centrifuge at >10,000 × g, and retain up to 50,000 J2s per 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

substeps.instruction: Collect J2s and place in 0.01 % Tween 20 solution.
Centrifuge at >10,000 × g and discard supernatant.
Retain up to 50,000 J2s in a 1.5 mL tube.
Remove residual liquid first with a P200 pipette, then with a P20 pipette.
Flash‑freeze the pellet in liquid nitrogen and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Homogenize and digest J2s
steps.instruction: Lyse the frozen J2 pellet with lysis buffer and proteinase K, then incubate to digest.

substeps.instruction: Add 20 µL lysis buffer to the frozen pellet and grind with a micro‑pestle for ~30 s until thawed.
Add 140 µL lysis buffer and 40 µL proteinase K; mix by inversion.
Incubate at 55 °C for 18 h, mixing gently but frequently.

steps.title: Remove RNA
steps.instruction: Treat the lysate with RNase A to degrade RNA.

substeps.instruction: Add 10 µL RNase A (10 mg mL⁻¹, Thermo Fisher Scientific) and incubate at room temperature for 5 min.
Label this tube as “tube 1”.

steps.title: First phenol‑chloroform extraction
steps.instruction: Extract aqueous DNA phase using phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume (~200 µL) of phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol to tube 1.
Vortex 1 min or rotate on a HulaMixer for 15 min (rotation preferred for HMW DNA).
Spin at >10,000 × g for 5 min.
Transfer ~180 µL of the top aqueous phase to a new tube (tube 2), avoiding the organic phase. Cut the tip of a P1000 tip if needed for gentle pipetting.

steps.title: Second extraction (back‑extraction)
steps.instruction: Recover additional aqueous DNA from the original phenol phase.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 µL elution buffer to the original tube 1 (still containing phenol/chloroform/isoamyl alcohol).
Vortex 1 min or rotate on a HulaMixer for 15 min.
Spin at >10,000 × g for 5 min.
Transfer ~180 µL of the top aqueous phase to tube 2, avoiding the organic phase.

steps.title: Third chloroform back‑extraction
steps.instruction: Remove residual phenol by a chloroform/isoamyl alcohol wash.

substeps.instruction: Add an equal volume of chloroform/isoamyl alcohol (~360 µL) to tube 2.
Vortex 1 min or rotate on a HulaMixer for 15 min.
Spin tube 2 at >10,000 × g for 5 min.
Transfer as much of the top aqueous phase as possible to a new tube (tube 3), avoiding the chloroform layer.

steps.title: Precipitate genomic DNA
steps.instruction: Precipitate DNA from the aqueous phase using ammonium acetate, glycogen, and ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Add NH₄OAc to tube 3 to a final concentration of 0.75 M.
Add 1 µL glycogen (20 mg mL⁻¹, Thermo Fisher Scientific).
Add 2.5 × volume of 100 % ethanol and mix well.
Spin at 4 °C, top speed, for 20 min.
Decant supernatant carefully without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Wash and dry DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA pellet twice with 80 % ethanol and dry.

substeps.instruction: Add 300 µL fresh 80 % ethanol, flick the tube, then spin at 4 °C, top speed, for 15 min.
Decant supernatant and repeat the ethanol wash.
Decant again and use a P20 pipette to remove residual ethanol.
Air‑dry the pellet for ~30 min.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Dissolve the dried pellet in elution buffer.

substeps.instruction: Add 25–30 µL elution buffer to the pellet.
Incubate overnight at 4 °C to allow complete resuspension.

steps.title: Assess DNA quality and quantity
steps.instruction: Measure purity and concentration of the extracted DNA.

substeps.instruction: Use a Nanodrop (Thermo Fisher Scientific) to record A260/280 (expected 1.8–2.0) and A260/230 (expected 2.0–2.2) ratios.
Quantify DNA with a fluorometric assay (e.g., Qubit) following the manufacturer’s protocol.
